summary.headline: Finolex Q1 FY27: volume fell 27% YoY to ~68,000 MT, while EBITDA rose 14% to INR107 crore and margin widened to 12%.
summary.overview: Volumes fell 27% YoY to about 68,000 MT as PVC price volatility triggered channel destocking, with April the weakest month and May and June growing per management. Revenue fell 27% to INR884 crore from INR1,043 crore, but EBITDA rose 14% to INR107 crore and margin improved from 9% to 12%, which management attributed mainly to top-line realization rather than cost. PAT was about INR107 crore and cash stood at INR2,636 crore. Management said July was the best month of the four, with a minimum price floor from the MIP and customs duty withdrawal, but declined to give full-year volume or margin guidance beyond reiterating the sub-15% margin view.

segments.name: Agri pipes
segments.commentary: Agri was 69% of volume; agri volume fell 27% YoY. Fittings were 5% of agri and 11% of total volume.

segments.name: Non-agri / plumbing
segments.commentary: Non-agri was about 25% of volume (fittings 25% within non-agri per management); volume fell ~24% YoY, versus ~18-20% industry peers per management.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: CPVC was about 7% of volume in Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 volume guidance; management said it is too early and will revisit after Q2 trends.
Margin: reiterated the Q4 FY26 view of sub-15% EBITDA margin, with no revision.
Management expects a somewhat better Q2 on realizations after the MIP-driven price floor; said it was hopeful H1 volume could be flattish YoY, with a plus possible if July's pace holds.

Capex: capital outlay of INR125-200 crore per year for expansion and debottlenecking, unchanged. Installed capacity 520 (unit as stated), FY26 volume 333, headroom for 10-12% growth over roughly the next 1-1.5 years.
Other income of ~INR75 crore in the quarter is mark-to-market and driven by bond yields, so it is not guaranteed to recur at that level.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity stated as 520 (units not specified); FY26 volume 333. Management says there is headroom to grow 10-12% over the next 1-1.5 years.
Growth is coming through debottlenecking, replacing lower-capacity extruders with higher-capacity ones, rather than large greenfield or brownfield projects.
Capex outlay remains INR125-200 crore, unchanged.

Ratnagiri PVC: EDC-based line running without interruption. VCM-based line does not run during the June-September monsoon months because the Ratnagiri jetty is fair-weather only. VCM availability is constrained by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints.
CPVC extrusion capacity is considered sufficient for near-term CPVC growth, according to management.
demand_pricing: Average PVC price in Q1 was about USD875/MT versus USD707/MT a year earlier (ICIS), carried over from elevated Q4 FY26 levels. A sharp intra-quarter correction in April triggered channel destocking.
Management cited INR96 to INR92 to INR82/kg as the PVC price path through April. Analyst cited a INR12-13/kg hike in the last 15-20 days after the MIP and duty changes.
Customs duty exemption on PVC resin was withdrawn in mid-July, and a minimum import price (MIP) was imposed. Management said these should support price stability and channel inventory.
Pass-through: management said almost all of the recent price increase (barring INR1-2) has been passed to customers.
Demand: July was the best month of the four, with a strong pickup; August to date was described as moving in the right direction.
Channel inventory is near normal, with some room left. A lot of stocking occurred in July in anticipation of price increases. Quantification in days was not given.
PVC-EDC spread was ~USD501/MT in Q1 FY27 versus ~USD522 a year earlier, and ~USD490 currently. PVC-VCM spread was INR122/kg in Q1 FY27 versus INR163 a year earlier.
Pricing: management said Finolex prices ~10-12% above Supreme-type peers in the market (ballpark only).
Market share: management said FY26 share of the top 5-6 reporting companies was about 22%, and it sees no change in Q1. An analyst cited FY23 share of about 27%.
JJM 2.0: management said the outlay is about INR67,000 crore, not higher than JJM 1.0. All sales go through channel partners, so there is no direct correlation to volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realization not rise QoQ when peers reported 7-9% jumps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realization per kg was up ~15% vs the same quarter last year and was in line with peers. It said Q4 FY26 was an aberration with a sharp price rise, and that falling PVC prices in April drove the QoQ result. Discounts and incentives also affect net realization.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the volume decline was agri vs non-agri, and what were the monthly trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri fell 27% and non-agri fell ~24% YoY. April was the weakest month, May grew and June was normal. Management did not give monthly figures and said it would reach out separately.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion despite falling volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin was largely top-line driven, with costs range-bound. It cited backward integration and the timing of raw material procurement as a cushion. It did not quantify inventory gains or losses.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year volume decline? Can H1 be flat YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide full-year volume. It said July was a good month and that flattish H1 YoY is possible, with a plus if July's pace holds, while August and September are still to be seen.

qa_highlights.question: Why not deploy the INR2,636 crore cash into CPVC capacity and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CPVC extrusion capacity is sufficient and CPVC is about 7-8% of the PVC pipe market, which Finolex matches. It said the Board decides on cash deployment or returns and will announce when a decision is made.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin guidance sub-15% when Q1 delivered 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is holding the sub-15% guidance from Q4 because of volatility in Q1 and wants another quarter of data before revising it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VCM supply situation and the PVC plant utilization outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VCM availability is limited by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints. The VCM line does not run during monsoon months (about June to September) because of the fair-weather jetty. Management said efforts to secure supply are ongoing and H2 is uncertain.
